Elena — appreciate the clear notes and the tax cert. A couple of commercial thoughts from our side: 

- Minimum commit: to accommodate your Q1 ramp, we can split the first-year commit into two tranches: 40% for Q1–Q2, then 60% for Q3–Q4 (billing as committed units monthly). This lowers the upfront pressure while preserving volume-based pricing.
- Pricing: if Skyline can firm to a 12-month committed ARR, we can hold the quoted unit price and include a ramp adjustment schedule in the Order Form.
- Net terms: we typically standardize on Net 45 for new enterprise partners with an annual commit. If Skyline needs Net 60, we’ll need to escalate to Sales Ops for an exception and update payment reserves.

If you agree to the tranche approach, we can prepare an updated Order Form with explicit tranche quantities and milestone invoicing. Irene — can you coordinate the doc update and legal handoff?

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Team — flagged a few finance items for legal and procurement to note: 

1) Invoicing entity: Redwood Inference, Inc. (US) will be the invoicing entity for US billing. We need to ensure the Order Form references the correct legal entity and address; please do not route invoices to an EU entity unless we have an intercompany arrangement.

2) Taxes: Skyline is responsible for sales tax/VAT where applicable. We require the tax residency certificate (received — thank you) and an explicit tax clause that places the burden of VAT on the customer unless Redwood is required to collect/withhold by local law. Marissa — please craft tightened language to avoid open indemnities.

3) Invoicing cadence & PO: We can support monthly invoices in arrears for committed units. Please confirm whether Skyline will provide a single annual PO referencing the tranche schedule or separate POs per tranche. We prefer a single PO with line items for each tranche to simplify collections.

4) Net terms: Net 45 standard for committed ARR. If Skyline requests Net 60, we will need a credit reserve hold for first invoice equal to one month’s average usage and approval by Finance.

Attaching: TaxGuidance_Redwood.pdf (internal guidance).

Karthik

Elena / team — I reviewed the redline and propose the following commercial/legal edits (high level):

1) Invoicing entity & PO: Order Form should state invoicing entity as "Redwood Inference, Inc., 1201 Market St, San Francisco, CA" and include a PO reference field; invoice will list PO number supplied by Skyline.

2) Net terms: agree to Net 45 tied to 12-month committed ARR. If Skyline mandates Net 60, we will accept only if a credit hold equal to one month’s committed spend is documented.

3) Taxes: revise tax section to state customer is responsible for all taxes, duties, and withholdings except Redwood’s income taxes. Add requirement that Skyline provide tax residency evidence prior to first invoice; if evidence is not provided, tax withholdings will be treated per law and Redwood may gross-up pricing if required. (We prefer to avoid open-ended indemnities.)

4) Minimum commit & tranche schedule: include explicit tranche table in Order Form with quantities, effective dates, and pro-rated invoice line items. Add a clause allowing a one-time mid-year adjustment with mutual written consent.

5) Governing law & dispute: suggest California (San Francisco) as governing law and small-claims / expedited dispute path for billing disputes under $25k.

I attached a marked version (OrderForm_Redline_Marissa.docx) with line-level edits. Happy to hop on a brief call to walk through.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
